'''Christopher Nicholas Duhon'''<ref>[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/chris_duhon/bio.html Chris Duhon] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081007223128/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/chris_duhon/bio.html |date=October 7, 2008 }}. NBA.com</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/39170/sid/2930/tid/379/_/2001_World_Championship_for_Young_Men/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151115055734/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/39170/sid/2930/tid/379/_/2001_World_Championship_for_Young_Men/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 15, 2015|title=USA 5 – Christopher Nicholas Duhon|website=[[FIBA]].com|access-date=January 26, 2020}}</ref> (born August 31, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Duhon was a [[point guard]] for the [[Duke University|Duke]] [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Blue Devils men's basketball team]] from 2000 to 2004. He then played for the [[Chicago Bulls]], [[New York Knicks]], [[Orlando Magic]], and [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

==College career==
In his senior year at [[Salmen High School]] in [[Slidell, Louisiana]], Duhon was voted [[Louisiana Mr. Basketball Award|Mr. Basketball]] for the state of [[Louisiana]],<ref>[http://www.hoopshype.com/players/chris_duhon.htm NBA Players – Chris Duhon]. HoopsHype, accessed on December 22, 2008</ref> made the [[McDonald's All-American Team]], and won the McDonald's Three Point Shootout.<ref>[http://www.sportsstats.com/duke/compare/mcdonald.html McDonald's All-Americans] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080331032933/http://www.sportsstats.com/duke/compare/mcdonald.html |date=March 31, 2008 }}. Sportsstats, accessed on December 22, 2008</ref>

Duhon arrived at Duke in 2000, where he was an important role player, playing backup to [[point guard]] [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jason Williams]]. Following the injury of teammate [[Carlos Boozer]], Duhon was placed into the starting lineup as point guard, with Williams moving to shooting guard, a combination in which Duhon played well. The Duke Blue Devils went on to win the 2001 national championship, defeating Arizona in the finals.

His sophomore season, Duhon again started in the Duke backcourt alongside fellow guard Jason Williams. That season, Duhon's reputation grew for his defense, court vision, and versatility as a point guard, averaging 2.3 steals per game, and 5.9 assists per game.

From his junior season on, Duhon became an instrumental leader for the Blue Devils. In the 2002–2003 season, he led a young Duke team to the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Sweet 16]], and averaged 9.2 points, 6.4 assists, and 2.2 steals per game and was among the top 10 assists leaders in NCAA Division I history.

In his senior season, Duhon averaged 10 points, 6 assists, 2.2 steals, and 4.1 rebounds per game, en route to another [[Final Four]].

Duhon finished his career as Duke's all-time leader in steals (300) and minutes played (4,813), and second in assists (819). He had one of Duke's top assists to turnover ratios as well. In Duhon's four years, Duke compiled a 123–21 record, making Duhon the second winningest player in Duke and [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] history, behind Duke's [[Shane Battier]] (131 wins). He helped the Blue Devils win three ACC Championships. Duhon was a finalist for the 2004 [[Wooden Award]], the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]], and [[Adolph Rupp Trophy|Rupp Trophy]] awards. He left as the only Atlantic Coast Conference player to record 1,200 points, 800 assists, 475 rebounds, 300 steals, and 125 three-point shots.

==NBA career==
===Chicago Bulls (2004–2008)===
[[File:Duhon pointing.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Duhon played with the Bulls from 2004 to 2008]]
In June 2004, Duhon was selected as the 38th pick in the [[2004 NBA draft]] by the Chicago Bulls. In his rookie season with the Bulls, Duhon played in all 82 games, averaging 5.9 points and 4.9 assists per game.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/duhonch01.html Chris Duhon Statistics]. Basketball-Reference, accessed on December 22, 2008</ref> Duhon's best game in his rookie year was against the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. Duhon led the Bulls in a comeback against the Hawks, where they trailed at the half. Duhon hit 8 of 9 three-point field-goals in the game, scoring 24 points. This was a franchise record before [[Ben Gordon (basketball)|Ben Gordon]], a fellow 2004 draft pick, hit nine threes the following season. The Bulls re-signed Duhon after matching an offer from the [[Toronto Raptors]] for the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]]. In the 2005–2006 season, Duhon averaged 8.7 points per game and 5.0 assists per game.

In 2005, after [[Hurricane Katrina]], Duhon's Stand Tall Foundation handed out over 3,000 boxes of supplies worth $450,000 for residents of his hometown [[Slidell, Louisiana|Slidell]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bulls/community/duhon_update_050922.html Duhon's Relief Efforts Yield over 3,000 Boxes of Supplies] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061130053743/http://www.nba.com/bulls/community/duhon_update_050922.html |date=November 30, 2006 }}. [[Chicago Bulls]], September 22, 2005, accessed on December 22, 2008</ref>

Duhon played a key role in the Bulls winning their first playoff series since the [[Michael Jordan]] era against the [[Miami Heat]]. The Bulls swept the Heat four games to zero. Duhon provided key minutes as the sixth man in the series against Miami, where he played more minutes because of the foul trouble [[Kirk Hinrich]] was plagued with throughout the series.

After the Bulls fell in a 3–0 hole, a deficit no team has come back from in the NBA Playoffs, Duhon played solidly off the bench. He hit a key three-pointer in Game 4 that forced the lead to 23 points. In a relatively easy Game 5 win, Duhon scored 8 points off of 2 threes and a driving lay-up.

The trade of [[Ben Wallace (basketball)|Ben Wallace]] and [[Joe Smith (basketball)|Joe Smith]] to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for [[Larry Hughes]] and [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]] also caused a logjam in the backcourt. He eventually found his way back into the rotation and once again proved to be a solid floor general. In a game against the [[Golden State Warriors]] on February 7, 2008, Duhon scored a career-high 34 points along with 9 assists, 3 steals, 2 rebounds, and 4 three-pointers. Duhon's contract expired June 30, 2008.

===New York Knicks (2008–2010)===
On July 4, 2008, Duhon accepted a two-year deal worth close to $12 million total to play for the New York Knicks.<ref>Deveney, Sean. [http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=431071 Knicks, Chris Duhon agree to 2-year deal] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080705193921/http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=431071 |date=July 5, 2008 }}. ''[[Sporting News]]'', July 4, 2008, accessed on December 22, 2008</ref> Though his other suitor, the [[Orlando Magic]], were considered a team more championship-built, he would have been a backup to [[Jameer Nelson]]. With the Knicks, he was considered a possible replacement to [[Stephon Marbury]],<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3473845 Duhon picks Knicks over Magic; agrees to two-year deal]. ESPN, July 7, 2008, accessed on December 22, 2008</ref> whose contract with the Knicks was bought out later that season.

On November 29, 2008, in a game against the [[Golden State Warriors]], Duhon set a new Knicks single-game record with 22 assists in one game.

===Orlando Magic (2010–2012)===
On July 8, 2010, Duhon signed a four-year deal worth a guaranteed $12 million with the [[Orlando Magic]].

===Los Angeles Lakers (2012–2013)===
On August 10, 2012, Duhon was traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] along with teammates [[Dwight Howard]] and [[Earl Clark]] as part of a four-team deal.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic_sign_duhon_070810.html | title=Magic Sign Free Agent Guard Chris Duhon | work =[[NBA.com]] | date=July 8, 2010 | access-date = July 9, 2010}}</ref> On June 29, 2013, Duhon was waived by the Lakers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/130629chrisduhon Lakers Waive Chris Duhon]</ref>

==Coaching career==
In April 2014, Duhon was hired by first-year head coach [[Dan D'Antoni]] as an assistant coach at [[Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball|Marshall]]. D'Antoni previously coached him as an assistant in New York and Los Angeles.<ref>{{Cite news | url=http://www.wsaz.com/video?videoid=2833042 | title=Chris Duhon talks Marshall Basketball (video) | publisher= WSAZ-TV | date=April 30, 2014 | access-date=May 12, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2050705-report-chris-duhon-takes-marshall-asst-gig | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517120206/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2050705-report-chris-duhon-takes-marshall-asst-gig | url-status=dead | archive-date=May 17, 2014 | title=Report: Chris Duhon Takes Marshall Asst. Gig | publisher= Bleacher Report | date=May 3, 2014 | access-date=May 12, 2014}}</ref>  After his 2015 aggravated [[Driving under the influence|DUI]] arrest, Marshall University's athletic department issued a statement saying Duhon has been suspended for a violation of department rules and policies.<ref name="HeraldDispatch">{{cite web | url=http://www.herald-dispatch.com/news/herd-asst-duke-standout-duhon-arrested-in-dui/article_e0b9704e-9773-11e5-9dad-a3e7dc9d2713.html | title=Herd asst, Duke standout Duhon arrested in DUI | publisher=herald-dispatch.com | date=November 30, 2015 | access-date=November 30, 2015}}</ref> On January 24, 2017, Duhon resigned from Marshall following an arrest for driving on a revoked license three days earlier.<ref name=GazetteMail>{{cite web | url=http://www.wvgazettemail.com/sports-marshall-university/20170124/marshall-basketball-assistant-coach-chris-duhon-resigns-following-saturday-arrest | title=Marshall basketball assistant coach Chris Duhon resigns following Saturday arrest | publisher=Charleston Gazette-Mail | date=January 24, 2017 | access-date=January 24, 2017}}</ref>

In 2023, Duhon was hired as head coach for the [[Gaston Christian School]] boys' basketball team.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bergin|first=Mark| url=https://www.wralsportsfan.com/duke-legend-chris-duhon-takes-on-new-role-as-high-school-basketball-coach-in-north-carolina/21003646/ | title=Duke legend Chris Duhon takes on new role as high school basketball coach in North Carolina | publisher=WRAL | date=August 17, 2023 | access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Duhon is the cousin of fellow basketball player [[Jarrett Jack]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jarrett_jack/bio.html |title=Jarret Jack Bio Page |work=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 28, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070213180254/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jarrett_jack/bio.html |archive-date=February 13, 2007 }}</ref> and [https://ca.movies.yahoo.com/neverleveled-culture-destination-festival-set-183903921.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAAFGNlDtt-p0vElMIFtkZGvFMSrsmfp6lCB7M3Mei8m_qeiyDZp0vSaB5aDFdnBEkvB_NR37FmY3q1zd1Lgh4A NeverLeveled's Founder and Live Entertainment] Producer Guy B Duhon Jr; Duhon is married to Andrea Hernandez, with whom he has 4 children.

===2013 automobile attack===
According to police reports, following an argument, Duhon was intentionally hit by an automobile in an [[Orlando, Florida]] parking garage. His head hit the car's windshield. Duhon was taken to a hospital and could not recall the incident. The driver escaped, and police are investigating the incident as [[aggravated battery]].<ref name="attack">{{cite news |url=http://www.myfoxorlando.com/story/23688725/police-former-orlando-magic-player-run-over-in-parking-garage |title=Police: Former Orlando Magic player hit by car in parking garage |last=Bristow |first=Holly |publisher=[[WOFL|WOFL FOX 35]] |date=October 14, 2013 |access-date=October 15, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016025325/http://www.myfoxorlando.com/story/23688725/police-former-orlando-magic-player-run-over-in-parking-garage |archive-date=October 16, 2013 }}</ref>

===Legal troubles===
On November 30, 2015, shortly after 6 AM police officers were asked to respond to a "man down" call and found Duhon passed out in the driver's seat of his Ford Escape.<ref name="complex.com">{{cite web | url=http://www.complex.com/sports/2015/11/chris-duhon-former-duke-star-found-passed-out-car-arrested-extreme-dui | title=Former Duke Star Chris Duhon Found Passed Out in His Car, Arrested for Extreme DUI | publisher=Complex.com | date=November 30, 2015 | access-date=November 30, 2015}}</ref> Duhon was booked into the Western Regional Jail in Barboursville, West Virginia on a charge of aggravated DUI.<ref name="arre.st">{{cite web | url=http://arre.st/WV-1005171159 | title=Christopher N. Duhon Sr. Aggravated DUI | publisher=Arre.st | date=November 30, 2015 | access-date=November 30, 2015}}</ref>  Marshall University's athletic department issued a statement saying Duhon has been suspended for a violation of department rules and policies.<ref name="HeraldDispatch"/>

On January 21, 2017, Duhon was arrested for driving on a revoked license stemming from his November 2015 DUI arrest, and 3 days later resigned from his assistant coaching position at Marshall.<ref name=GazetteMail/>
